content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.
When this app is finished, what should be easier or different for you than it is today?

Honestly, right now saving a link is a mess for me. I've got bookmarks scattered everywhere — some in my browser, some emailed to myself, some I just lose track of. So what I really want is one place where I can save a link and actually find it again later.

A few things I picture:

- When I come across something worth keeping, I want to save it quickly — paste in the web address, and maybe give it a title so I remember what it is.
- Later, I want to see everything I've saved in a list, and be able to open any of them back up.
- If I saved something by mistake or don't need it anymore, I want to remove it.
- I collect a lot of these, so I need to be able to search or filter to find the one I'm thinking of, rather than scrolling forever.
- Some way to group or tag them would help — like keeping work links separate from recipes.
- And if I try to save the same link twice, I'd expect it to be smart about that rather than showing me two copies.

That's the gist of the pain I'm trying to solve. Does that give you enough to start with?

Open the [duplicate-check prototype](http://maker:4001/?duplicate=1), paste `https://example.com/#about`, and save it. Confirm whether keeping the count at one and focusing **Example Domain** is right when the address only adds a jump-to-section ending.

I’ve assumed trailing slashes and jump-to-section endings do not make a new bookmark, while address additions that can select genuinely different content remain distinct.

Yes, that's the right call. A jump-to-a-section ending like that still points at the same page as far as I'm concerned, so it shouldn't create a second copy — keeping the count at one and taking me to the Example Domain I already saved is what I'd want. And I agree with the distinction: if the address genuinely points at different content, that's a separate bookmark and should be treated as its own. This handles it sensibly.

Open the [single-bookmark collection](http://maker:4001/?single=1). Remove **Example Domain** through its `•••` menu, then click **Undo**.

Confirm whether briefly showing the friendly empty collection at zero, followed by restoring the bookmark and count to one, is the right behavior when the last saved item is removed by mistake.

Yes, that behaves just how I'd want. Removing my last link drops me to the friendly "nothing saved yet" state at zero — which is honest, that's really where I am for a moment — but the Undo still brings the bookmark and the count right back to one when I realize I didn't mean to delete it. Good to know the safety net works even when it's the only thing left in my collection.

content:
So far, five feature flows are settled across 17 approved scenarios:

- Save links with automatic details, sensible fallbacks, and duplicate protection
- Browse and open a clear newest-first collection
- Remove links through the item menu with an eight-second Undo
- Search instantly across bookmark details without capitalization sensitivity
- Organize with overlapping tags, reusable suggestions, and duplicate-tag prevention

The important empty, invalid, failed-lookup, no-result, and last-item cases are also settled.

May I start implementing this scope?

Yes, please go ahead and start building this. That summary captures what we've worked through, and I'm comfortable with it as the scope for this first version.

One thing I want to make sure carries into the build, since it's the whole reason I wanted labels: being able to actually click a label and have my collection narrow to just those links. We looked at that when we compared the folder-versus-labels idea, so I'm assuming it's part of what you're building — I just want to see it working with the real thing.

The finished app is ready at [http://maker:4000](http://maker:4000).

Verification passed across all 17 approved scenarios, 10 internal tests, the full browser workflow, external page-detail lookup, and desktop/mobile layouts. This explicitly includes clicking a bookmark’s label to narrow the real collection.

Everything we settled together is here, and you've confirmed it all holds up. I'm happy to call this the finished first version.
